title: Gon
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: Gon, a tiny but unbeatably strong dinosaur living long after the dinosaur age, wanders the wilderness looking for food, sleep or solitude and gets tangled up in the lives of other animals. The stories are episodic and told entirely without dialogue or sound effects, in detailed naturalistic art.
life_message: Living freely and boldly in nature, and standing up for smaller creatures against bullies, is a good life.

content.note: Encounters range from friendly to violent and Gon wins every fight against bigger foes (Wikipedia; Viz blurb on defending from the mean and hungry).
Predators and wilderness peril, played for comedy.
Slapstick fighting by an animal; little to imitate.

Dignity vs honor.evidence: Gon answers challenges from bigger animals personally and always wins (Wikipedia).

Order vs freedom.evidence: Gon roams alone and does as he likes in the wilderness.

Civic vs kin.evidence: No family; helps whichever creature he meets.

Equality vs hierarchy.evidence: No social order; strength alone, but no ranks.

Tradition vs secular-rational.evidence: Neither custom nor reason; animal instinct.

Survival vs self-expression.evidence: Food, sleep and survival drive most chapters (Wikipedia).

folkways.japan: Wordless seinen manga from Kodansha's Morning, reflecting a Japanese tradition of detailed nature illustration and visual gag comedy.

delivery.evidence: Told without words; reviewers praise universal visual storytelling (Wikipedia reception).

winners_losers: Gon always wins against bigger bullies; sympathy goes to small, friendly creatures he protects.
